title: Good to Great: Why Some Companies Make the Leap... and Others Don't
author: Jim Collins
target_audience: Anyone interested in organizational transformation and success
primary_purpose: To identify and explain the key factors that enable certain companies to transition from being merely good to achieving sustained greatness, based on empirical research and case studies.

structure_format.narrative_style: Analytical, research-driven, and accessible with storytelling elements
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters focusing on core concepts (e.g., Level 5 Leadership, the Hedgehog Concept, Culture of Discipline, etc.)
features: In-depth analysis of companies over 15-year periods
Comparative case studies (good-to-great companies versus comparison companies)
Key concepts summarized with diagrams and visuals

key_concepts_lessons: Level 5 Leadership: The importance of humility and fierce resolve at the top.
First Who, Then What: Putting the right people on the bus before setting strategy.
Confront the Brutal Facts: Creating a climate of truth while retaining hope.
The Hedgehog Concept: Focusing efforts at the intersection of passion, best at, and economic engine.
Culture of Discipline: Merging entrepreneurial drive with disciplined thought and action.
Technology Accelerators: Using technology as a tool, not a driver, of greatness.
The Flywheel Effect: Building momentum through consistent effort over time rather than one big breakthrough.
notable_features: Based on rigorous, five-year research project analyzing 1,435 companies
Identifies seven core characteristics of companies that make the leap to greatness
Extensive use of comparative analysis and real-world case studies
Models and concepts widely adopted in business and leadership communities
cultural_historical_context: Released in the early 2000s, 'Good to Great' was published during a time of economic growth and corporate scrutiny, with a focus on long-term sustainability and value creation. Its research-driven approach responded to previous business fads and the need for evidence-based insights.
reception_impact: International bestseller, translated into dozens of languages
Highly influential in shaping leadership and management thinking in the 21st century
Adopted as required reading in MBA programs and executive training
Praised for actionable insights and practical frameworks
Some criticism regarding post-publication performance of certain 'great' companies and survivorship bias
comparable_titles: Built to Last: Successful Habits of Visionary Companies by Jim Collins and Jerry I. Porras
The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephen R. Covey
In Search of Excellence by Tom Peters and Robert H. Waterman Jr.
The Innovator's Dilemma by Clayton M. Christensen
